- When sentiment is positive (≥0.33) and forecast is below recent high, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and forecast is above recent high, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast to avoid overshoot.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price after a spike in sentiment (e.g., 0.67) — apply a +0.5 to +1.0 adjustment to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Model overestimates in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days) when sentiment is neutral or negative — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0 to early forecast points.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >+1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.3–0.7; if <–1.5σ, increase by 0.3–0.7.  
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive 0.00 values, model tends to underestimate — add 0.5–1.0 to forecast mean.  
- Overshoot correction: if forecast peaks >+2.0 above true peak in 30d, reduce by 0.5–1.0 in next 7d forecast to avoid overcorrection.
